review_candidates.description: At MMS we're proud of our history, our heart, and our commitment to making a difference to people's lives. We care because people matter. We collaborate because the greatest achievements are made together, and we continuously create because some of the best innovations have yet to be imagined. Here’s how you will make a difference in this role… As the Workforce Planning Specialist you will be responsible for translating forecast demand into workforce plans, roster strategies and staffing models that support service delivery, workforce efficiency and operational objectives across Maxxia and RemServ Operations. This role owns workforce scheduling, availability planning, leave governance and compliance, ensuring workforce supply aligns to forecast demand through effective roster design, capacity planning and workforce mix management. You will provide leaders with clear insights and recommendations on workforce risks, leave trends, utilisation, roster effectiveness and productivity opportunities, while partnering with workforce specialists to support compliant, sustainable and operationally effective plans. At MMS clear expectations help our people Be the Difference. Your key responsibilities in this role will include: Develop workforce plans, roster strategies and staffing models aligned to forecast demand, service requirements and operational priorities. Design and maintain master rosters, shift patterns and workforce structures that balance customer demand, employee experience and cost outcomes. Manage workforce availability, leave governance and capacity frameworks, monitoring risks and recommending actions to maintain service performance. Develop contingency and surge plans while ensuring workforce plans, schedules and rostering practices comply with awards, legislation, policies and WFM requirements. Monitor overtime, workforce compliance, planning controls and system configuration to maintain roster integrity and support effective operational and financial outcomes. Partner with Operations leaders and the Workforce Management team to provide practical workforce planning advice, insights and recommendations. Identify opportunities to improve workforce utilisation, roster effectiveness, flexibility and workforce planning practices. Support operational and strategic workforce initiatives that improve planning maturity, service delivery and workforce performance. To be considered for this role you will have: Experience in workforce planning in a complex multi-site, multi-channel operational environment. Strong understanding of workforce planning principles, scheduling methodologies and workforce optimisation practices. Understanding of workforce planning concepts including shrinkage, adherence, coverage and interval staffing. Experience balancing workforce supply, demand, service outcomes and labour costs. Strong analytical skills with the ability to identify workforce risks and recommend practical workforce planning solutions. Experience translating workforce forecasts into workforce plans, roster strategies and staffing requirements. Understanding of performance metrics, workload drivers and operational planning. Knowledge of Australian employment legislation, workforce compliance obligations and award-based rostering environments. What we can offer you: Strong culture and the support of a values-based recognition program Novated leasing benefits and discounts 12 weeks paid parental leave Comprehensive learning and development opportunities to support your career growth Sonder digital wellbeing platform , providing personalised support 24/7, plus annual flu vaccinations Default Income Protection Insurance reimbursed for members of the MMS Default Super Fund Exempt Employee Share Plan Volunteer leave & Career break MMS Rewards program Embracing our value of Everyone Matters we hold a collective commitment to foster an environment where all differences are valued and respected. We encourage individuals from all backgrounds including Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander peoples, those caring for someone or living with a disability, LGBTQIA+ and culturally diverse applicants to apply. We value the skills and attributes veterans can bring to our organisation. We embrace hybrid working and welcome conversations about flexibility. Please note all successful candidates will undergo background checks (including criminal history and ASIC checks) and an NDIS Workers Screening Check if appropriate. All information provided will be treated confidentially. We acknowledge Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander people as the Traditional Custodians of the lands where we live, learn and work. If you identify as a person living with disability and require adjustments to our recruitment process, please contact us at mmsgrouprecruitment@mmsg.com.au

review_candidates.title: UAS Flight Operations - Germany
review_candidates.description: Who We Are Helsing is a defence AI company. Our mission is to protect our democracies. We aim to achieve technological leadership, so that open societies can continue to make sovereign decisions and control their ethical standards. As democracies, we believe we have a special responsibility to be thoughtful about the development and deployment of powerful technologies like AI. We take this responsibility seriously. We are an ambitious and committed team of engineers, AI specialists and customer-facing programme managers. We are looking for mission-driven people to join our European teams – and apply their skills to solve the most complex and impactful problems. We embrace an open and transparent culture that welcomes healthy debates on the use of technology in defence, its benefits, and its ethical implications. The role As nominated postholder for Germany, you will build lean operational processes that let Helsing iterate fast without compromising the safety and legal standards required to operate in a demanding regulatory environment. You will act as the named individual accountable to the LBA for flight operations and safety in Germany, working in close partnership with the Accountable Manager to ensure every mission, trial and demonstration meets the requirements of EASA Regulation (EU) 2019/947 and 2019/945 as transposed under the LuftVG and LuftVO. This role sits at the intersection of field oversight and regulatory compliance, translating SORA methodology and LBA requirements into practical, auditable processes across programmes. You will be based in Germany, with frequent travel to trial and demo sites. The day-to-day Design and continuously improve flight safety processes that scale with operational tempo, keeping the German operations manual and supporting procedures lean and proportionate rather than bureaucratic Own and maintain the German operations manual and LBA authorisation, updating SORA assessments in line with the current EASA methodology and any LBA-specific supplements Act as the primary point of contact with the LBA, in German, for authorisation matters, occurrence reporting under Regulation (EU) 376/2014, and audits Conduct site recces and pre-flight risk assessments, primarily for German trial and demo locations, with occasional travel to other Helsing operating locations as required Manage safety events locally: capture, investigation, corrective action and closure, feeding into the group-wide safety management system Deliver internal training and maintain crew competency records to the standard required under the operations manual Provide field oversight of flight operations, with delegated authority from the Accountable Manager Run the German compliance monitoring programme and report findings to the accountable manager on a fixed schedule You should apply if you Have built or re-engineered operational processes in a fast-scaling environment, balancing compliance rigour with speed of delivery Have developed and applied flight safety expertise across complex, regulated environments Have successfully delivered compliance or safety management projects from initiation through to completion Understand EASA Regulation (EU) 2019/947 and 2019/945 and their transposition under the LuftVG and LuftVO Have experience interacting with the LBA or an equivalent EASA national competent authority Communicate clearly and build effective relationships with diverse stakeholders, including national authorities and internal programme teams Note: We operate in an industry where women, as well as other minority groups, are systematically under-represented. We encourage you to apply even if you don't meet all the listed qualifications; ability and impact cannot be summarised in a few bullet points.
